question.text: Himalayan Debt AIF has 30% of its corpus contributed by a single NBFC (RBI-regulated). Under the SFA implementation standards (per SEBI Oct 2024 circular), specific due diligence is triggered to prevent evergreening. The threshold of RBI-regulated investor's corpus contribution that activates this DD is:

answer.text: 25% of corpus or more (either individually or through a same group of investors)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI's Oct 8, 2024 Circular on Specific DD for evergreening: RBI-regulated investors (e.g., Banks, NBFCs) who individually OR along with a same group of investors contribute MORE than 25% of the corpus of the AIF Scheme trigger specific DD (per SFA implementation standards) BEFORE making investments. Also triggered if such RBI-regulated investors are associates of Manager/Sponsor, or have majority/veto power in the Investment Management Committee. Look-through applies for AIF-in-AIF or GIFT City fund investors. **The Trap:** Options A/B understate. Option C uses the 50% threshold that applies to QIB/QB benefit circumvention and land-border DD (different triggers). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers all four SFA DD scenarios: (I) QIB via AIF, (II) QB via AIF, (III) RBI-evergreening (25%), (IV) land-border (50%). Don't confuse the percentages — each scenario has its own trigger. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Maintain a 'DD trigger matrix' updated at every capital call: for each LP, tag [QIB status, QB status, RBI-regulated status, BO land-border status] and track cumulative corpus contribution. Any LP moving past a trigger triggers a fresh DD cycle plus custodian reporting.
